## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to blend core Unix tools to process mixed-format logs, including gzipped files, without external dependencies. It also checks per-service aggregation and case-insensitive deduplication.

## Key Concepts
- find/xargs streaming of files with -mmin for the 6-hour window

```bash
  xargs -0 -I{} sh -c 'zcat {} 2>/dev/null || cat {}' | \
  awk '/ERROR:/ {msg=$0; gsub(/^[ \t]+|[ \t]+$/,"",msg); print msg}' | \
  sort -iu | wc -l
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to parse mixed log formats, traverse hierarchical logs, handle gz archives, and enforce a time window with robust aggregation. It also exercises building production-like one-liners and validating correctness across edge cases.

## Key Concepts
- File traversal with find
- On-the-fly decompression (gz)
- Dual-format parsing (text and JSON)
- Time-window filtering with epoch conversion
- Top-N aggregation

## Code Example
```bash
find /logs -type f \( -name "*.log" -o -name "*.log.gz" \) -print0 | \
  xargs -0 -I{} sh -c 'case "{}" in *.gz) zcat "{}" ;; *) cat "{}" ;; esac' | \
  awk -v cutoff=$(date -d '12 hours ago' +%s) '
  match($0, /^\[([0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2} [0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2})\] ([^:]+): (.*)/, a) {
    cmd = "date -d \"" a[1] "\" +%s"
    cmd | getline ts
    close(cmd)
    if (ts >= cutoff && a[2] == "ERROR") { messages[a[3]]++ }
  }
  match($0, /"ts":"([^"]+)".*"level":"ERROR".*"msg":"([^"]+)"/, a) {
    cmd = "date -d \"" a[1] "\" +%s"
    cmd | getline ts
    close(cmd)
    if (ts >= cutoff) { messages[a[2]]++ }
  }
  END {
    for (msg in messages) print messages[msg], msg
  }' | sort -nr | head -5
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to reason about log-stability and data integrity across plain and JSON formats, including gzipped rotated files, using only standard tools.

## Key Concepts
- Looping over multiple service dirs
- Handling plain text and JSON lines
- Decompressing gzip with gzip -t and zcat
- tail -c to inspect last byte
- POSIX shell compatibility considerations

## Code Example
```javascript
for d in /logs/service-*/; do
  s=${d##*/}; s=${s%%/*}; p=0
  for f in "$d"/*.log "$d"/*.log.gz; do
    [ -f "$f" ] || continue
    if gzip -t "$f" 2>/dev/null; then c=$(zcat "$f" | tail -c 1); else c=$(tail -c 1 "$f"); fi
    if [ -n "$c" ] && [ "$c" != $'\\n' ]; then p=1; break; fi
  done
  [ "$p" -eq 1 ] && echo "$s:PARTIAL" || echo "$s:CLEAN"
done | sort
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you adapt to multiple active symlinks per service?
- How would you validate this in a CI with synthetic partial-lines?

A single agent runs under a file lock to serialize execution, tail -F follows the log through renames/rotations, and an offset file records the last processed line to resume safely. Batch processing reduces CPU usage and ensures atomic offset updates.

- **Rotation Handling**: tail -F remains connected across log rotations
- **Stateful Processing**: persistent offset avoids reprocessing after restarts
- **Idempotent Queueing**: include a monotonic id per line to detect duplicates
